text: Jim stood in the back of the advanced yoga studio, sweating profusely as he attempted to mimic the instructor’s effortless downward dog. The room was silent, save for the soft hum of meditation, until Jim’s stomach gave a loud, ominous gurgle. Trying to ignore it, he shifted his weight, only to produce a sound remarkably similar to a deflating balloon. The class froze. The instructor, a serene woman named Serenity, turned slowly. "Jim," she said gently, "perhaps you should focus on your breath, not your... emissions." Jim, flustered, tried to laugh it off but ended up knocking over a stack of mats. As he scrambled to pick them up, he accidentally bumped into a large, stuffed animal prop in the corner—a giraffe, the animal known for its long neck. The giraffe’s head tilted down, staring directly at Jim with judgmental eyes, as if to say, "I have a long neck, but I don't make noises like that." The class erupted in laughter, breaking the zen completely. Jim sighed, realizing that while he couldn't control his body, he could at least blame the giraffe.
